factual_findings: Documented CLI build-training invokes the Rust build_training binary, whose producer uses FastSubgraphEngine.
Fast-engine node times are quantized to integer generations, but candidate rank is UNCAPPED absolute quantized-time difference, not log2. Matrix log2 encoding is separate.

Candidate distance ties use reference-vector index. The documented Rust producer derives this vector from HashMap iteration, so its order is not a recovered stable roster order. A prospective reproducible comparison must capture/freeze one actual native vector before labels and reuse it across eligibility variants.
Default max_train_subgraphs and max_val_subgraphs are None. Producer engine max_count is0. It collects all eligible labelled native rows before per-query1024/512 chunk construction.

Native training row retention depends on the resolver. With first_snp and no purity filter, absence of observed SNPs can drop intervals. Root common-midpoint supervision must not fabricate extra context labels to imitate this. Full observed inference context can be retained with supervision-100 outside exact shared targets, disclosed as common-target adaptation.
Shared100k-only rows substantively thin GRU context. The sealed old adapter is retained for audit and must not support a current-native baseline performance claim.
April paper25reference+3ancestor architecture is a separate unavailable paper-era implementation, not the documented current15reference+0ancestor transformer/BiGRU code.
Current advanced defaults set3epochs. The old adapter20epoch maximum is an explicit prospective finite choice, not the current default or a recovered paper hyperparameter.
old_packet_classification: development shared-row legacy-sampler adaptation, not author-faithful current fast-producer baseline
